To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the performance of the Discrete Wavelet Transformation is not justified by its computational burden, (b) the SVM classifier is the only classifier that consistently achieves top performance in combination of each feature extraction method and (c) the SVM classifier in combination with the Discrete Wavelets Transform outperforms all other classifiers in combination with all feature representations.

(i) simple features can be sufficient to obtain good classification performance, (ii) a Support Vector Machine is a suitable classifier for surface electromyography-based hand movement classification, and (iii) the performance of the best performing classifier and feature extraction method is not significantly affected by the number of classes.
